module-2-study-checker-project.label: Module Project: Build a Study Checker
module-2-study-checker-project.summary: Build one study checker cumulatively: read a score, classify it, add a membership rule, handle a missing code first, then finish with invalid input and ordered score statuses. Every step starts from the exact previous solution.

mp-1-check-pass-fail.title: Step 1: Classify the score
mp-1-check-pass-fail.prompt: Keep the existing score input. Add the first rule: print `Passing` when the score is at least 70; otherwise print `Needs practice`.
mp-1-check-pass-fail.hint: Add an `if` / `else` beneath the existing score input.

help.concept: This step adds the checker's first decision without replacing its existing input setup.

0.message: Keep the score input and add `if score >= 70:` with an `else` fallback.

mp-2-check-join-rule.title: Step 2: Add the membership rule
mp-2-check-join-rule.prompt: Keep the score checker exactly as your starting point. Read one more line into `member`. A learner can stay `Passing` only when the score is at least 70 **and** `member` is `yes`. If `member` is not `yes`, print `Join club first`. Otherwise print `Needs practice`.
mp-2-check-join-rule.hint: Add `member = input()`, then combine the passing requirements with `and`.

help.concept: This step extends the existing score decision with a second required condition.
help.hint_1: Use `score >= 70 and member == "yes"` for the first branch.
help.hint_2: Check `member != "yes"` before the remaining score fallback.

0.message: Read `member` and use `score >= 70 and member == "yes"` before the membership fallback.

mp-3-handle-missing-text.title: Step 3: Handle a missing code first
mp-3-handle-missing-text.prompt: Keep the checker you already built. Read a third input into `code`. If `code` is the empty string, print `Missing code` before any normal membership or score result. Otherwise preserve the existing rules.
mp-3-handle-missing-text.hint: Add `code = input()` and place the empty-code branch before the existing decision chain.

help.concept: This step adds a sentinel case before the broader rules while preserving their behavior for non-empty codes.
help.hint_2: Move the previous first condition to `elif` so only one result prints.

0.message: Read `code` and put `if code == "":` before the existing checker rules.

mp-4-build-final-study-checker.title: Step 4: Finish the study checker
mp-4-build-final-study-checker.prompt:
Keep the same three inputs and existing missing-code rule. Add the final ordered decisions:

- `Missing code` if `code` is empty
- `Invalid score` if `score` is less than 0
- `Join club first` if `member` is not `yes`
- `Excellent` if `score` is at least 90
- `Passing` if `score` is at least 70
- `Needs practice` otherwise

Only one message should print.
mp-4-build-final-study-checker.hint: Keep special and invalid cases before the broader score ranges.

help.concept: The final checker combines sentinel handling, validation, membership, and narrower-before-broader score rules in one ordered chain.
help.hint_1: After the missing-code check, reject negative scores before normal status decisions.
help.hint_2: Check `score >= 90` before `score >= 70` so excellent scores are not hidden by the broader passing range.

0.message: Keep the three inputs and order the final chain as missing code, invalid score, membership, excellent, passing, fallback.

try-module-2-study-checker-project-sketc.title: Set up the score input
try-module-2-study-checker-project-sketc.prompt: Start the study checker by reading one integer score into a variable named `score`.
try-module-2-study-checker-project-sketc.hint: Use `int(input())` so later steps can compare the score numerically.

help.concept: The cumulative project begins with the input that every later score rule will reuse.
help.hint_2: Do not print a status yet; this preview only establishes the shared starting point.

try_module_2_study_checker_project_sketc.title: Try it yourself
try_module_2_study_checker_project_sketc.prompt: Read one score. Print `Ready` if it is at least 50. Otherwise print `Keep going`.
